senses.gloss:
Adbhuta
śaiva. Upāgama in Dīptāgama. See list in Kāmika.

Adbhutagītā
vedānta. by Dattātreya. B. IV. 36. Is it Avadhūtagītā ?

Adbhutagītā
or nAnakagItA poem in 8 adhyāyas, purporting to be by Nānak. Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 405.
--C. Kaiśavapada by Keśavānandasvāmin.
Ed.. of 1901, ibid. 1892-1906. 405.

Adbhutacarita(tra)
spoken by Śiva; means of removing the evil effects of portents. L. 250. Tagore 57.

Adbhutataraṅga
a prahasana by Harijīvanamiśra, son of Lālamiśra, the son of Gauḍa Vaidyanāthamiśra; written a. the behest of King Rāmasiṁha of Jaipur, A. D. 1635-89. Bikaner 3122-25 Rep. Rāj. & C. I. p. 52.
For a. account of it, see Samskrita Ranga Annual, Madras, IV. 1966. p.. 35-39.

Adbhutataraṅgiṇī
jy. by Balabhadra. K. 222. Oudh V. 30.

Adbhutatāṇḍavamantra
MD. 15247.

Adbhutadarpaṇa
or adbhutasaGgraha jy. based on Ballālasena's Adbhutasāgara, by Mādhava, son of Raghunātha. AS. p. 7. Hpr. I. 3. IO. 3105. Kāṭm. 3. 11. Mithilā III. 5. NW. 78. RASB. III. 2579.

Adbhutadarpaṇa
nāṭaka in 10 acts. based on the Rāmāyaṇa. by Mahādeva, son of Kṛṣṇa Sūri of Kauṇḍinya gotra an. pupil of Bālakṛṣṇānanda. Adyar. Adyar [Page116-b] D. V. 1230-1231 (both inc.). Burnell 167a. Oppert I. 3941. II. 7470. PUL. II. p. 279. Sūcīpattra 25. TD. 4534. Trav. Uni. 8831.
Pt.. K. M. 55.

Adbhutadharmaparyāya
Bud. Sūtra. AMG. II. p. 279. AR. XX. p. 476. Nanjio 260. 261 (the two are similar transl.. of the first an. seventh chs. of Nanjio 259 “the Sūtra of highest reliance”). 400.

Adbhutadharmaparyāya_(?)
(‘Adbhutahetupratyaya sūtra’). Bud. Sūtra. Nanjio 400 C.. AMG. II. p. 279 an. AR. XX. p. 476.

Adbhutanirūpaṇa
jy. Mithilā.

Adbhutanirṇaya
jy. Dharmanāth Sastri, Assam 33.

Adbhutapañjara
nāṭaka by Nārāyaṇa, son of Raṅgaśāyi Dīkṣita, an. pupil of Tippā Dīkṣita an. Rāmabhadra Dīkṣita. Adyar. Adyar D. V. 1232. Sucīndram 89. TCD. 1240A. 1473. Tra. Ad. Rep. 1103, 123. Trav. Uni. T512A. C1606C. 5552. Triv. Cur. I. 222.
Pt.. TSS. 210. 1963.

Adbhutapañjarakathā
a metrical resume of the story of the above play by the a.'s father Raṅgaśāyi Dīkṣita. (Yajñendra). TCD. 1240. Trav. Uni. T512B (inc.).

Adbhutapadmāvatīkalpa
Jain. stotra. by Candrasūri.
Pt.. in Comparative an. Critical Study of Mantraśāstra, Sri Jain Kala Sahitya Samsodhak Series 1. App. p.. 1-14.

Adbhutapuṇya
or adbhutaphulla poet. Smv. p.. 192 (“Āyāte dayite” is q. in Bhoja's Sarasvatīkaṇṭhābharaṇa an. in the Daśarūpāvaloka). 277 (Adbhutapuṇya's is given a. Adbhutaphulla's in Sbhv. 1588. 2076. In Śp. the same is Adbhutapuṇya's a. in Smv.). Śp. [Page117-a. 3528. 3680 (Adbhutapuṇya in both cases).

Adbhutabrāhmaṇa
the concluding part of the Ṣaḍviṁśabrāhmaṇa. Alph. List Beng. Govt. p. 3. Bik. 109. Trav. Uni. 1988B.
Ed. separately by Weber, Berlin 1859.

Adbhutamayūrapuccha
on portents. by Jīvanakṛṣṇa Mukhopādhyāya.
Pt.. Cooch Behar 1914. Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 429.

Adbhutamahāśāntyādi
from Av. RASB. II. 1415 (i).

Adbhutayoga
yoga. Bik. 1218.

Adbhutarāghava
nāṭaka by Vanamālimiśra. Rep. Hpr. 1895-1900, p. 19.

Adbhutarāmāyaṇa
or adbhutottararAmAyaNa or adbhutottarakANDa a. if it is book VIII of the Rāmāyaṇa; ascribed to Vālmīki; owing to difference in ch. division, mss. have 20, 26 an. 27 chs. See analysis in Weber p. 123 an. note in RASB. V. 3206.
The Bombay edn. is in 27 chs. Pt.. a. Benares also, 1881.
On its chs. on music, see J. of the Music Academy, Madras, XVI. p.. 65-72.

Adbhutaviveka
appeasing of supernatural phenomena. by Mahīdhara. NW. 174.

Adbhutaveṅkaṭeśastuti

Adbhutaśānti
67th pariśiṣṭa of the Av. in 8 sections. Mu7nchen 183 (72). Tb. 214 (67th). Weber 366 (67th). See p.. 432-7, p.. 2, Leipzig edn. of the Av. pariśiṣṭas by Bolling an. Negelein.
--Mu7nchen 183 (76) describes a. Ad. śānti in 22 sections, but this is correctly Gārgyāni, LXXb of the above ptd. edn.

Adbhutasāgara
